tagline: A mountain village on the slopes of the Karkas range, Isfahan province, Iran

distances.source: Kojaro gives both '15 km east' and 'Meymeh borders on the west'

location.route: From the Shahin Shahr to Meymeh road, turn off about 50 km north of Shahin Shahr at Dehlor, then pass Bidshak. Soh is at the end of the road. There is no bus terminal or railway station in the village.

populationNote: Kojaro says about 1,000 people are in the village in spring and summer (seasonal residents for 7 to 8 months). This is not a census figure.

facts.label: Language
facts.value: Persian, with a local dialect (not yet documented)

history.text: Said to be more than 2,000 years old. Evidence cited: castles with Gabri (Zoroastrian-era) names, the Nachaft castle, the Qal'eh Miyan, millstones and the ruins of a fire temple. FA Wikipedia states that no documents support the age.
The name is said to come from 'sohi' or 'sahi', meaning tall or high, because the village sits on the slopes of the Karkas (کرکس) mountains.
The caravan road made the village a trading and resting point until the middle of the Qajar era. Surviving buildings date from the Safavid and Qajar periods.
Until 1996 (1375) the village belonged to Natanz County, then was separated.

landmarks.name: Soh Caravanserai
landmarks.text: A stone inscription on the portal dates it to 1223 AH (1808 CE), in the reign of Fath-Ali Shah Qajar, with the builder named as Abolqasem Esfahani. About 3,000 m², four iwans and 20 rooms around a courtyard. National monument no. 7641 (registered 17 Esfand 1381). Restored 1395 to 1400 with local donations.

landmarks.name: Imamzadeh Yusuf
landmarks.text: Shrine in the upper village, about 400 years old, with a 16 m dome in turquoise tile. Said to be the resting place of Yusuf, son of Imam Hadi.

landmarks.name: Imamzadeh Golileh
landmarks.text: Turquoise-domed shrine in the lower village, at its centre.

landmarks.name: The old bath
landmarks.text: A Qajar-era bath about 200 years old. Of the upper and lower baths, one survives, restored with local help.

landmarks.name: Kadkhoda house
landmarks.text: Home of the village headman, Mirza Bahram Safavi.

landmarks.name: Nav Bridge
landmarks.text: Kojaro names it and gives no age, material or condition.

landmarks.name: Imamzadeh mill
landmarks.text: One of three water mills named by Kojaro. IRIB (2018) and Hamaseh Sazan say seven mills; Hamaseh Sazan says they are ruined, but that page's coordinates do not match, so the ruin is not settled. Do not guess the location from the name.
landmarks.source: Kojaro; IRIB News, 14 Shahrivar 1397; Hamaseh Sazan

landmarks.name: Mirza Abolhasan mill
landmarks.text: Named by Kojaro. Who he was, and the mill's condition, are not written.

landmarks.name: Mirza Mohammad mill
landmarks.text: Named by Kojaro. The three names and IRIB's seven mills are not reconciled.

landmarks.name: The telegraph house
landmarks.text: Kojaro: an old mansion known as the telegraph house, counted among Safavid and Qajar remains. Later called the English telegraph house. May be the same building as the Farangi mansion.
landmarks.source: Kojaro; Hamaseh Sazan; Saed News, Feb 2026

landmarks.name: Dovecote tower
landmarks.text: Kojaro lists one tower and does not say where it is or whether it is intact.

landmarks.name: Mirza Jafar's house
landmarks.text: Named by Kojaro. No link is given to the kadkhoda or to the mill names.

landmarks.name: Brick kiln
landmarks.text: Named by Kojaro, with no other detail.

landmarks.name: The small zurkhaneh
landmarks.text: Kojaro says traditional gym sports are popular and that a small zurkhaneh is used for them.

landmarks.name: The mosque beside the bath
landmarks.text: Earlier notes said a mosque about 200 years old beside the bath. Kojaro does not describe it. The 200 years belongs to the bath, so the number may have been copied by mistake. IRIB's Friday mosque may or may not be the same building.
landmarks.source: Site notes checked against Kojaro and IRIB News

landmarks.name: The Abbasi caravanserai
landmarks.text: Kojaro: an Abbasi caravanserai on the main road into the village, evidence of a trade route. A 2026 IRNA summary calls it Agha Kamal Payin and translates it Abbasid, which is not the same word. Not the caravanserai inside the village.

landmarks.name: The Farangi mansion
landmarks.text: Not a separate Kojaro entry. Hamaseh Sazan says it was the telegraph office. A 2026 summary quoting IRNA lists it apart from the English telegraph house.

landmarks.name: The covered passage in the upper-castle alley
landmarks.text: A sabat (covered lane) placed by a 2026 IRNA summary in the old upper-castle neighbourhood. Kojaro does not describe it. Original IRNA text not read.

landmarks.name: Kandeh Baghestan
landmarks.text: A 2026 summary says “Kandeh garden”. Kojaro does not list it. Meaning, place and whether it is a garden are not recorded.

places.name: Kuh-e Char
places.text: Kojaro spells it کوه چر, beside Baghal Siyah. No height or path. The village, not the peak, is given as 2,350 m.

places.name: Kuh-e Baghal Siyah
places.text: Named by Kojaro next to Kuh-e Char, with no other description.

places.name: Lab Char river
places.text: Named by Kojaro. A seasonal river on the west side is described separately and is not treated as the same river. Farm water is mostly surface streams; a place called Band collects water for two or three fields.

places.name: Qash Sorkheh
places.text: Named by Kojaro. What a qash is here, and where it is, are not said.

places.name: Margaleh
places.text: Named by Kojaro and Persian Wikipedia. Neither says what kind of place it is.

places.name: Sar-Marq meadow
places.text: Kojaro: مزرعه سرمرق (مرغه‌زار). Earlier site spelling سرمرغ was the source's سرمرق. Size and place not given.

places.name: Gazi meadow
places.text: Persian Wikipedia lists it with no citation. Kojaro does not. Not the Gazi dialect of Gaz.

places.name: Haz spring
places.text: Named by Kojaro. Persian Wikipedia's Gol Pardeh Haz is a separate list entry and is not identified as this spring.

places.name: Paymil plain
places.text: Named by Kojaro. Size and access not given. Spring and early summer are the better time to walk the plains.

places.name: The waterfall
places.text: Persian Wikipedia lists the word only, with no height, season, path or citation. Kojaro does not name it.

places.name: Sarkarriz
places.text: Named on Persian Wikipedia's tourism line with no description. Kojaro does not list it.

places.name: Gol Pardeh Haz
places.text: Listed by Persian Wikipedia apart from Kojaro's Haz spring. The two are not identified as one place.

places.name: Hol Haramzadeh
places.text: Name only on Persian Wikipedia's tourism line. Not said whether it is a person or a place. Kojaro does not list it.

places.name: Nachaft
places.text: Named as a tourist spot with no description. History notes also cite a Nachaft castle ruin for the village's age and say that age has no document. The two are not identified. Sources spell it نچفت; the site had also written ناچفت.

places.name: Zir-Pol
places.text: Named by Persian Wikipedia. Which bridge, and whether it is below Nav Bridge, is not said. Kojaro does not list it.

livelihood.summary: About 86% of residents worked in agriculture in a survey from 2007 to 2008: crops 56%, livestock 27%, beekeeping 2.4%, poultry 0.8%. Homes are spread out, far from the fields and orchards. Water comes mainly from surface streams. In wetter years lentils, chickpeas, beans and saffron are also mentioned (FA Wikipedia).
livelihood.apples: The apples are described as among the best in Isfahan province, and about 30% of the village's economic capacity is apple growing.
crafts: Hand-woven carpets in the Joshaqani style, sold in Isfahan and Tehran

traditions.text: On Tasua, during Muharram, the village carries a palm-shaped standard (nakhl-gardani). It is decorated in the morning at Imamzadeh Yusuf, carried to Imamzadeh Golileh, and returned after the Ashura noon mourning. Other rituals include alam-gardani, ammar-gardani, taziyeh and nowheh chanting. Kojaro says these mourning rituals are about 200 years old and were listed in Iran's national intangible heritage (no. 1207) on 5 Mordad 1395. The amari (a small wooden bier-frame, kept by one family) is carried on the 8th; seven standards (five coloured, two black) lead the palm on Tasua; chest-beating and dirges start on the first night (Mehr News, single source). Local foods: kalleh-joosh, kashk-e mama, tanoori abgoosht, golmisheh, shami, semnu.

people.note: Only people with a source. Behzad Ghaderi, Lotfollah Khadem Sohi, Yousef Bakhshizadeh Sohi, Farshid Navabi Sohi and Seyed Farhad Sohi appear on FA Wikipedia only; no second source was found, and one report says FA Wikipedia does not even link Ghaderi to Soh, so they are not published.

list.name: Seyed Ali Safavi Sohi
list.text: Born 29 July 1940; commanded the 293rd tank battalion; killed by shrapnel 2 August 1983 (place differs by source: Fakkeh or Jangal-e Amqar). Father Seyed Musa Safavi. A Tehran bridge carries his name. Whether he is from this Soh is medium confidence (FA Wikipedia, Khabar Foori Mar 2021).

list.name: Mirza Bahram Safavi
list.text: Village headman; his house is a historic site (Kojaro).

list.name: Abolqasem Esfahani
list.text: Builder named on the caravanserai inscription (Kojaro).

toVerify: Coordinates: EN Wikipedia's infobox (31.78 N, 51.37 E) is about 200 km away from every other source (33.44 N, 51.45 E). The second value is used here.
Distance and direction to Meymeh (15 km east vs borders on the west).
Whether the village really has about 1,000 people in summer.
The 2,000-year age and the 1996 transfer from Natanz.
Whether the Instagram page soh_village is active and who runs it.
Seasonal population: Kojaro says ~1,000 in spring/summer, Gardeshnama says up to 5,000 (Nowruz, Muharram, summer).
Distance to Meymeh/Shahin Shahr: Kojaro says 15 km, 65 km and 75 km in different places.
Caravanserai: inscription says Fath-Ali Shah (1223 AH = 1808 CE), but its style looks Safavid to several writers; the registry no. 7641 is not confirmed outside Kojaro.
Intangible heritage no. 1207 (Kojaro): not confirmed elsewhere.
Saray-e Moallem eco-lodge is in Tarq Rud (Natanz County), not near Soh.
The Rijksmuseum CC0 photo 'View of the town of Soh' (Sevruguin) may show a different Soh; not used.
Sources not opened: IRIB News 3114741, Tasnim 2840223 and 1445378, touristgah.com Soh page.
Registry no. 7641 'Soh Caravanserai (Qajar)': Kojaro says Isfahan, 17 Esfand 1381; Persian Wikipedia's caravanserai list puts the row under Ardabil province. Check the national heritage register.
